Trusses

Source: R/physics-continuum-truss.R
Truss.Rd

Truss() is a plane truss of nodes joined by members. $add_node(), $remove_node(), $add_member(), $remove_member(), $change_node_label() and $change_member_label() build it; each takes any number of tuples, such as list(label, x, y) for a node and list(label, start, end) for a member. $apply_load(list(node, magnitude, direction)) adds a load with the direction in degrees, $apply_support(list(node, type)) a "pinned" or "roller" support, and $solve() finds the reaction loads and the internal forces. The properties are $nodes, $node_labels, $node_positions, $members, $member_lengths, $supports, $loads, $reaction_loads and $internal_forces. $draw() draws the truss with base R graphics. After sympy.physics.continuum_mechanics.truss.

Usage

Truss()

Value

A Truss object.

Examples

t <- Truss()
t$add_node(list("A", 0, 0), list("B", 2, 2), list("C", 3, 0))
t$add_member(list("AB", "A", "B"), list("BC", "B", "C"), list("AC", "A", "C"))
t$apply_load(list("B", Symbol("P"), -90))
t$apply_support(list("A", "pinned"), list("C", "roller"))
t$solve()
t$reaction_loads
#> {R_A_x: 0, R_A_y: P/3, R_C_y: 2*P/3}
